sources.summary: Investigative feature (12 January 2018) on the plight of transgender women in French prisons: incarcerated on the basis of legal gender status, most trans women housed in all-male facilities because placement follows the sex on the ID document (Article D248 of the criminal procedure code separates men and women only); first-person accounts (a trans woman held in a northern correctional facility in 2014 shouted at by other detainees; another foreign trans woman detained after a publicised 2016 Paris protest trial); the controller-general of places of deprivation of liberty says transgender detainees - the majority of whom are women - are the group that 'suffers the most' in prison.

Opinion of 25 May 2021 of the controller-general of places of deprivation of liberty (unofficial English translation) on the treatment of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty: serious violations of fundamental rights persist across all detention settings, based on some forty referrals since 2010, interviews with trans associations and European experts, observations from the interior, justice and health ministries, and on-site/document inspections; recommendations extend to intersex and non-binary persons; follows an initial 2010 opinion on transsexual prisoners.

Torture-prevention consortium blog (edited interview with the French national preventive mechanism): trans persons deprived of liberty face a constant risk of violence, discrimination and abuse; a new Opinion (25 May 2021) was needed because the 2010 Opinion covered only incarcerated trans persons and because detention conditions had not improved despite new gender-recognition laws; the new Opinion extends to all places of deprivation of liberty and to intersex and non-binary people, based on a decade of letters from detained trans people, ministry and association input and exchanges with European experts.
